title: SemVer range resolver accepts improper prereleases
statement:
# SemVer range resolver (`src/semver.mjs`)

The module implements semantic versions (SemVer 2.0.0) and package-manager-style ranges. Users report that `maxSatisfying([...], '^1.2.3')` sometimes returns a release candidate of the next major version instead of the highest compatible stable version. The whole module must obey the contract below; fix it without changing the API.

## Versions

- `parse(str)` → `{ major, minor, patch, prerelease, build, version }` or `null`.
  - Format `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH[-PRE][+BUILD]`, with surrounding whitespace ignored and an optional leading `v`. Non-string or invalid format → `null`.
  - `MAJOR`, `MINOR`, `PATCH`: integers without leading zeros (`0` is valid, `01` is not).
  - `PRE`: non-empty identifiers separated by `.`, each made of `[0-9A-Za-z-]`; digit-only identifiers cannot have a leading zero and become `number` in `prerelease`; the others stay as `string`. `BUILD`: likewise, but leading zeros are allowed and all stay `string`.
  - `version` is the canonical form `M.m.p[-pre]`, **without** build and without `v`.
  - `parse('v1.2.3-alpha.1+build.5')` → `{ major: 1, minor: 2, patch: 3, prerelease: ['alpha', 1], build: ['build', '5'], version: '1.2.3-alpha.1' }`; `parse('1.2.3-01')` → `null`; `parse('1.2')` → `null`.
- `valid(str)` → `parse(str).version` or `null`.
- `compare(a, b)` → `-1 | 0 | 1` by SemVer precedence; accepts strings or objects from `parse`; invalid string → `TypeError`.
  - Compares major, minor, patch numerically. With an equal tuple, a version **without** prerelease is greater than one with prerelease.
  - Between prereleases, identifiers are compared one by one: two numeric ones numerically; two alphanumeric ones by ASCII code order (`'B' < 'a'`); numeric is always **lower** than alphanumeric. If all common identifiers are equal, the one with more identifiers is greater.
  - Build is ignored: `compare('1.0.0+a', 'v1.0.0+b')` → `0`.
  - E.g.: `1.0.0-alpha < 1.0.0-alpha.1 < 1.0.0-alpha.beta < 1.0.0-beta < 1.0.0-beta.2 < 1.0.0-beta.11 < 1.0.0-rc.1 < 1.0.0`; `1.0.0-1 < 1.0.0-alpha`.
- `sort(versions)` → a **new** array with the original strings in ascending order of precedence; ties (same precedence, e.g. different builds) keep the input order; the input is not changed; any invalid item → `TypeError`.
  - `sort(['1.0.0+b', 'v1.0.0', '0.9.0', '1.0.0+a'])` → `['0.9.0', '1.0.0+b', 'v1.0.0', '1.0.0+a']`.
- `bump(version, kind)` → canonical string (build discarded); unknown `kind` → `RangeError`.
  - `'major'`: if the version is a prerelease with `minor === 0 && patch === 0`, returns `M.0.0`; otherwise `(M+1).0.0`.
  - `'minor'`: if it is a prerelease with `patch === 0`, returns `M.m.0`; otherwise `M.(m+1).0`.
  - `'patch'`: if it is a prerelease, returns `M.m.p`; otherwise `M.m.(p+1)`.
  - `'prerelease'`: without prerelease → `M.m.(p+1)-0`; with prerelease → increments the last identifier if it is numeric, otherwise appends `.0`.
  - `bump('2.0.0-rc.1', 'major')` → `'2.0.0'`; `bump('1.2.3', 'prerelease')` → `'1.2.4-0'`; `bump('1.2.3-alpha', 'prerelease')` → `'1.2.3-alpha.0'`.

## Ranges

`parseRange(str)` → array of sets (joined by OR); each set is an array of comparators `{ op, semver }` (intersection, AND), with `op ∈ '<' | '<=' | '>' | '>=' | '='` and `semver` an object like the one from `parse`. Non-string → `TypeError`; invalid syntax → `SyntaxError`.

- Sets are separated by `||`. Within a set, comparators are separated by spaces; spaces between an operator and its version are ignored (`'> 1.2.3 < 2'` ≡ `'>1.2.3 <2'`). An empty set (or whitespace only) ≡ `>=0.0.0`.
- **Partial version**: `X`, `X.Y` or `X.Y.Z[-PRE][+BUILD]` (with optional `v`), where each component may be a number or a wildcard `x`, `X` or `*`; omitted components count as wildcards. A number cannot come after a wildcard (`1.x.3` → `SyntaxError`); prerelease is only allowed with all three components numeric (`1.2.x-beta` → `SyntaxError`). More than three components, an operator without a version, etc. → `SyntaxError`.
- Expansion (always generates only the comparators shown, in this order):
  - full version without operator or with `=` → `=M.m.p[-pre]`; with `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=` → the comparator itself.
  - without operator/`=` and partial: `*` → `>=0.0.0`; `1` / `1.x` → `>=1.0.0 <2.0.0`; `1.2` / `1.2.*` → `>=1.2.0 <1.3.0`.
  - partial `>=`: `>=*` → `>=0.0.0`; `>=1` → `>=1.0.0`; `>=1.2` → `>=1.2.0`.
  - partial `>`: `>*` → `<0.0.0` (nothing satisfies); `>1` → `>=2.0.0`; `>1.2` → `>=1.3.0`.
  - partial `<`: `<*` → `<0.0.0`; `<1` → `<1.0.0`; `<1.2` → `<1.2.0`.
  - partial `<=`: `<=*` → `>=0.0.0`; `<=1` → `<2.0.0`; `<=1.2` → `<1.3.0`.
  - Tilde `~`: `~*` → `>=0.0.0`; `~1` → `>=1.0.0 <2.0.0`; `~1.2` → `>=1.2.0 <1.3.0`; `~1.2.3[-pre]` → `>=1.2.3[-pre] <1.3.0`.
  - Caret `^` (does not change the leftmost non-zero component): `^*` → `>=0.0.0`; `^1` / `^1.x` → `>=1.0.0 <2.0.0`; `^0.x` → `>=0.0.0 <1.0.0`; `^1.2.3[-pre]` → `>=1.2.3[-pre] <2.0.0`; `^0.2.3` → `>=0.2.3 <0.3.0`; `^0.0.3` → `>=0.0.3 <0.0.4`; `^0.0` and `^0.0.x` → `>=0.0.0 <0.1.0`; `^1.2` → `>=1.2.0 <2.0.0`.
  - Hyphen `A - B` (can only be the whole set; requires spaces around the `-`): lower bound `>=A` with missing/wildcard components filled with `0` (the prerelease of `A` is kept). Upper bound: full `B` → `<=B`; `B` = `X.Y` → `<X.(Y+1).0`; `B` = `X` → `<(X+1).0.0`; `B` = `*` → no upper bound.
- `formatRange(range)` (string or result of `parseRange`) → comparators written as `op + version` separated by one space, sets separated by `' || '`.
  - `formatRange('1.2 - 2.3')` → `'>=1.2.0 <2.4.0'`; `formatRange('1.2.3')` → `'=1.2.3'`; `formatRange('^1.2 || ~0.4.1')` → `'>=1.2.0 <2.0.0 || >=0.4.1 <0.5.0'`; `formatRange('')` → `'>=0.0.0'`.

## Satisfaction and selection

- `satisfies(version, range)` (`range` a string or already parsed; an invalid range propagates the error): invalid version → `false`. The version satisfies the range if it satisfies **some** set. It satisfies a set if:
  1. it passes all comparators of the set (by `compare` precedence); and
  2. if the version has a prerelease, there is **in the same set** at least one comparator whose version **also has a prerelease** and has the same `major.minor.patch` as the tested version. (So prereleases only get in when the range explicitly mentions them for that tuple.)
  - `satisfies('1.2.3-beta.2', '>=1.2.3-beta.1 <1.3.0')` → `true`; `satisfies('1.2.4-alpha', '>=1.2.3-beta <2')` → `false`; `satisfies('1.2.3+build', '=1.2.3')` → `true`; `satisfies('2.4.0', '1.2.3 - 2.3')` → `false`.
- `maxSatisfying(versions, range)` / `minSatisfying(versions, range)` → the **original** string of the highest/lowest version in the list that satisfies the range, or `null`. Invalid strings in the list are ignored. On a precedence tie, the one that appears **first** in the list wins.
  - `maxSatisfying(['1.2.3+b', 'junk', 'v1.2.3', '1.2.0'], '~1.2')` → `'1.2.3+b'`; `minSatisfying(['1.2.3', '1.2.0+x', '1.2.0'], '1.2.x')` → `'1.2.0+x'`.

bugs.summary: prerelease rule in testSet accepts any comparator with the same M.m.p tuple, without requiring the comparator's version to also have a prerelease (e.g.: 2.0.0-rc.1 satisfies ^1.2.3 via <2.0.0)
